From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Rodeo, rodéo, and rodeó

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
rodeo
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

From Spanish rodeo, from rodear (“to surround”), which refers to a cattle roundup.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /ˈɹəʊ.di.əʊ/
  • (General American) IPA(key): /ˈɹoʊ.di.oʊ/, /ɹoʊˈdeɪ.oʊ/
  • Audio (UK):(file)

Noun

[edit]

rodeo (plural rodeos)

  1. A gathering of cattle to be branded.
  2. (sports) A North American sport involving skills with horses, cows and other livestock.
  3. An entertainment event associated with the sport.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • antirodeo
  • been to the rodeo
  • brodeo
  • buffer rodeo
  • goat rodeo
  • mudeo
  • not one's first rodeo
  • roadeo
  • rodeo clown
  • rodeoer
  • rolleo

Translations

[edit]
sport

    Mandarin: 牛仔競技 / 牛仔竞技 (niúzǎi jìngjì)
  • Czech: rodeo (cs) n
  • Esperanto: rodeo
  • French: rodéo (fr) m
  • German: Rodeo (de) m or n
  • Hindi: रोडियो m (roḍiyo)
  • Japanese: ロデオ (rodeo)
  • Korean: 로데오 (rode'o)
  • Navajo: ahóóhai, naaʼahóóhai aleeh
  • Plautdietsch: Rodeo m
  • Polish: rodeo (pl) n
  • Portuguese: rodeio (pt) m
  • Russian: роде́о (ru) n (rodɛ́o)
  • Spanish: jaripeo (es) m, rodeo (es) m
  • Swedish: rodeo (sv) c
  • Turkish: rodeo (tr)

Verb

[edit]

rodeo (third-person singular simple present rodeos, present participle rodeoing, simple past and past participle rodeoed)

  1. (intransitive) To perform in a rodeo show.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • doore

Spanish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /roˈdeo/ [roˈð̞e.o]
  • Rhymes: -eo
  • Syllabification: ro‧de‧o

Etymology 1

[edit]

Deverbal from rodear.

Noun

[edit]

rodeo m (plural rodeos)

  1. detour (a diversion or deviation from one's original route)
    Synonym: desvío
  2. an instance of talking around or circumventing
  3. (sports) rodeo (North American sport involving skills with horses, cows and other livestock)

Swedish

[edit]
Swedish Wikipedia has an article on:
rodeo
Wikipedia sv

Noun

[edit]

rodeo c

  1. a rodeo

Usage notes

[edit]

"It's not my first rodeo" can be idiomatically translated as "Jag/man har (väl) varit med förr" ("I have been involved/participated before (haven't I?)" with the activity implied). "Det är inte min första rodeo" also occurs as a loan.

Declension

[edit]
Declension of rodeo
nominative genitive
singular indefinite rodeo rodeos
definite rodeon rodeons
plural indefinite rodeor rodeors
definite rodeorna rodeornas

  • “rodeo”, in Svenska Akademiens ordbok [Dictionary of the Swedish Academy] (in Swedish)
